skill.name: test-driven-development
skill.description: Guides agents through test-driven development for features, bug fixes, and refactors by requiring a failing test before implementation.
skill.summary: Apply red-green-refactor with verified failing tests before code changes.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: Static command findings were false positives from Markdown fences and inline examples, not executable Ruby or shell backtick evaluation. The zip archive contains only the same SKILL.md content, so the binary review finding is resolved. One semantic risk remains: the prose tells agents to delete code without requiring user confirmation.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before deleting, rewriting, or discarding existing code. Prefer reversible patches or backups when starting over.
Clarify that agents should inspect the project test tooling before running commands, and should follow local tool permissions.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Code Deletion Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to delete implementation code and start over when code was written before tests. Without an explicit confirmation step, this can cause loss of user work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The deletion instruction is explicit and repeated, including "Delete means delete" and "Delete code. Start over with TDD." The risk is bounded by TDD context, so medium severity is appropriate.

content.value_statement: Tests written after implementation can miss weak assertions and hidden behavior gaps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through failure-first red-green-refactor checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides agents to write a failing test before implementation.
Defines red, green, and refactor checkpoints.
Provides examples of focused tests and minimal implementation.
Lists checks for failure reasons and clean test output.
Explains when to ask a human before skipping TDD.
Offers troubleshooting guidance for hard-to-test code.
limitations: It does not detect the correct test framework automatically.
It does not run tests without the agent using local tools.
It may be too strict for prototypes without user approval.
It does not replace project-specific testing standards.

use_cases.title: Build Feature Tests First
use_cases.description: Plan one behavior, write the failing test, implement minimal code, and rerun the focused test.

use_cases.title: Prove Bug Fixes
use_cases.description: Create a regression test that fails on the bug before adding the smallest fix.

use_cases.title: Refactor with Confidence
use_cases.description: Use existing and new tests to keep behavior stable while cleaning implementation details.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill. Help me add [feature] by first writing one failing test, then minimal code, then refactor.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Bug with a Regression Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill to fix [bug]. Start with a regression test that fails for the current behavior, then implement the smallest fix.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Without Changing Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill for [refactor]. Identify protected behavior first, confirm tests cover it, then refactor while keeping the suite green.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Step TDD Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill for [multi-step change]. Split the work into behaviors, verify each failing test, implement minimally, and track refactor opportunities.

output_examples.input: Use TDD to fix empty email submissions.
output: Proposes a failing regression test for empty email validation.
Runs the focused test and confirms the failure reason.
Adds minimal validation and reruns the relevant tests.
Summarizes any cleanup after the tests pass.

output_examples.input: Add retry behavior to failed operations.
output: Defines the expected retry behavior in one failing test.
Implements only the retry path needed for that test.
Checks the passing test before suggesting refactor options.
Identifies behavior that must remain stable.
Checks whether tests already protect that behavior.
Adds focused tests before changing the implementation.

best_practices: Run the smallest relevant test first, then the broader suite.
Verify each new test fails for the expected reason before implementation.
Ask for confirmation before deleting or rewriting existing user work.
anti_patterns: Writing implementation code before a failing test exists.
Keeping untested code as a reference while writing tests.
Changing tests to match incorrect implementation behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill write tests before code?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs the agent to create a failing test before implementation and verify the failure reason.

faq.question: Can I skip TDD for prototypes?
faq.answer: Only with user approval. The skill treats prototypes and generated code as exceptions that need human confirmation.

faq.question: Does it choose my test framework?
faq.answer: No. It expects the agent to follow existing project tools and test conventions.

faq.question: Will it run shell commands?
faq.answer: It suggests local test commands. Tool permissions and user approval still control whether an agent runs them.

faq.question: Does it help with bug fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for a regression test that reproduces the bug before the fix.

faq.question: Is it safe for legacy code?
faq.answer: Use caution. Add tests around current behavior and confirm before deleting or rewriting existing code.
